fact: The Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation, at a working session with Meta in Ebene on 7 October 2026, discussed proposed amendments to the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021, which it treats as the operating legal framework for online content.
The National Crime Agency Bill text published by the National Assembly defines cybercrime by reference to offences under Part III of the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021.

The Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 (Act No. 16 of 2021) was passed by the National Assembly on 19 November 2021, assented to on 24 November 2021 and gazetted as Legal Supplement 567; the document's retrieval note says it was proclaimed in force on 10 December 2021, and it repeals the Computer Misuse and Cybercrime Act.
Minister Avinash Ramtohul said the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act would be reviewed to address certain offences while strengthening protection of freedom of expression.

ICT Minister Avinash Ramtohul said the existing Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act defines a fake profile, bans its use to cause harm on pain of 20 years' imprisonment and a one million rupee fine, and obliges platform administrators to moderate misleading content.
The Director of Public Prosecutions' April 2024 newsletter cites the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act 2021 as the law under which obscene deepfakes made with intent to harm carry criminal penalties.
The Ministry of ICT's sovereign cloud RFI names the Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act (CCA) 2021 among the local regulatory compliance standards suppliers are to implement.
